Bio

man lemi

Lemi Orhan Ergin is a Turkish software developer who describes himself as a software crafter. He is a co-founder and the Chief Software Crafter of Craftgate, a payment orchestration platform based in Istanbul, and the founder of the Software Craftsmanship Turkey community. He has been writing software since 2001.

Early life and education

Lemi is from İzmir, on Türkiye's Aegean coast. He studied computer engineering at Marmara University in Istanbul, where he earned a bachelor's degree in 2002 and a master's degree in 2005.[1] His first job, in the summer of 2001, was as a software engineer at TÜSSİDE, and in 2002 he worked as a laboratory assistant at the university.[1]

Career

After a year at BYM, Lemi joined Sony in 2004, where he spent most of the following decade.[1] His roles there ran from software engineer to technical coordinator and Scrum Master, principal software engineer, technical lead, solution architect and agile practice lead. He left Sony twice and came back both times: from 2006 to 2007 he served as a software officer in the Turkish Air Force, and in 2012 he spent six months at GittiGidiyor, eBay's marketplace in Türkiye.[1] He started working in Scrum teams in 2008, and in 2009 he trained as a Certified ScrumMaster with James Coplien.[1]

In 2015 he became a managing partner of ACM, a consultancy, where for two years he coached and trained teams at dozens of companies in agile culture and engineering practices.[1] In 2017 he joined iyzico, an Istanbul payments company, as Agile Practice Lead, and led the cultural transformation of its engineering team around agile and lean thinking and software craftsmanship.[1]

In April 2018 he co-founded Craftbase with Hakan Erdoğan, Sabri Onur Tüzün and Murathan Özcan, a company that built fintech and payment software for clients.[2] Craftgate grew inside it as a product and was introduced publicly in January 2021 as a cloud payment gateway that connects an online merchant to its banks and payment providers from one place.[2] In 2021, with investors and buyers at the door, the founders pursued neither and gave up their profitable service work instead; since January 2022 the company has been only Craftgate.[3] It raised a seed round in 2022,[4] took investment from Hepsiburada and D4 Ventures in 2023[5] and from Turkven in 2026,[6] and started operating in Spain in 2024.[7] Lemi is its Chief Software Crafter. The Craftgate page tells that story in full.

Community

In 2014 Lemi founded Software Craftsmanship Turkey, a community for developers who care about their craft, which has run more than 200 free meetups.[8] He has facilitated code retreats since 2013, including the Global Day of Coderetreat.[8] From 2015 to 2017 he was a community lead of Agile Turkey, which held more than 50 free public meetups in that time, and the product owner of the Agile Turkey Summit in 2015 and 2016 and of CraftSummit 2015.[8]

He was part of the team that translated the Agile Manifesto into Turkish, and he is the Turkish translator of the Software Craftsmanship Manifesto, the SOA Manifesto and the Disciplined Agile Manifesto.[8] The Community page has the links.

Speaking and sharing

Lemi speaks about software craftsmanship, engineering culture, agile without the ceremony, and Git. Outside Türkiye his stages include Devoxx in Belgium, Poland and Ukraine, XP Days Ukraine, GrowIT in Serbia, ITAKE in Romania, Agile Tour Kaunas, Bosnia Agile Day and Agile Middle East in Dubai, and at home he is a regular at DevFest Istanbul, DevFest İzmir, Java Day Istanbul and the Devnot Developer Summit.[9] He has also given more than 200 seminars at companies and universities.[9] In 2019 he gave a TEDx talk in Turkish, at TEDxTarsusAmericanCollege, on the night the root bug made him known.[10]

He hosts the Turkish podcast Lemi'nin Not Defteri, publishes his slides on Speaker Deck, and wrote for InfoQ on slowing down to go faster in software development.[11] The Talks page lists the talks year by year and on a map, and the Sharing page lists everything else.

The macOS root bug

On 28 November 2017 Lemi asked Apple Support on Twitter whether it knew that anyone could log in as “root” on macOS High Sierra with an empty password.[12] He had not discovered the flaw himself: the infrastructure staff at the company he worked for had come across it and reported it to Apple five days earlier, as he wrote the next day.[12] The tweet was covered around the world, from TechCrunch and CNBC to China Daily and the Turkish dailies,[13] and on 29 November Apple released Security Update 2017-001 and apologised to Mac users.[14]

He answered the criticism that he should have told Apple privately first in a talk on the ethics of going public, “Irresponsible Disclosure: Short Handbook of an Ethical Developer” (2018),[15] and told the story again in his TEDx talk.[10] The root bug page tells it in full.

Personal life

Lemi lives in Istanbul with his wife, an academic in the Computer Engineering Department of Marmara University, and their two sons. An İzmir native, he supports Göztepe, the İzmir football club.
